Powerful and gripping, this modern Antigone is laser‑focused on the cost—and the moral necessity—of refusing to acquiesce to power.

The production moves between striking clarity and a kind of thoughtful drift as we watch this dynamic new version of Antigone stand before us so authentically honest, raw, and sure of herself, holding our attention even as it resists a more defined shape.
Despite some disconnect of the two plotlines, the play does hold the audience’s attention but that was more due to the performer's abilities rather than the script itself.
The cast mostly delivers, but the allegory wobbles.
There is a powerful ninety-minute play about bodily autonomy and state power buried inside “Antigone (This Play I Read in High School).”

cn.t: Ziegler's bold feminist retelling reimagines Antigone through the lens of reproductive rights to mixed results. Critics praise its timely relevance and performances, but many find it overexplained, lacking dramatic tension, and struggling to fully cohere.

vr.q: Anna Ziegler's Antigone, this play I read in high school, hit me on every level.
I enjoyed this play quite a bit despite its occasionally flawed execution.
